headline: Deep models design DNA binders and PROTAC linkers while epistasis gains are challenged
label: Learned Sequence Representations
summary: Learned sequence and structure models are now generating binders and linkers, and benchmarks are testing what these models actually learn.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of learned sequence representations for molecular design and evaluation, rather than for predicting predefined labels alone. A pipeline combining RFdiffusion3 with AlphaFold3 off-target screening designed sequence-specific DNA binding proteins, with 7 of 15 targets bound. A benchmark of deep generative models for PROTAC design compared PROTAC-specific and general linker models on 40 experimental protein-ligand complex structures. A masked language model trained on DNA libraries after partial enrichment yields latent representations that quantify information evolution during binding selection. In contrast, an analysis of MULTI-evolve found that its multimutant predictions track an additive model and that its neural networks show no epistasis learning beyond additive baselines. What is new is the shift from label prediction toward generating structures and quantifying selection state, paired with more stringent tests of what these models have learned. The architectures and tasks differ, so this thread dominates rather than unifies all four items.
